a2-unit-17.17.1 Call 1:
Lucy: Hello? Tom's phone.
Kate: Hi, Lucy! It's Kate. Is Tom there?
Lucy: Hi, Kate! Hang on a minute, I'll get him. Tom? Tom? Sorry, he can't come to the phone. He's in the shower.
Kate: Oh, OK. Can you tell him that he left his jacket at the bakery? It's the black one. Did you get that?
Lucy: Yes. His black jacket is at the bakery. I'll pass that on.
Kate: Thanks! He can pick it up tomorrow morning. Bye!
Lucy: Bye!
a2-unit-17.17.2 Call 2:
Receptionist: Hello, Lakeview Hotel. Linda speaking. How can I help you?
Kate: Hello. Could I speak to Mr. Bennett, please?
Receptionist: Who's calling, please?
Kate: It's Kate Miller, from Sweet Kate Bakery.
Receptionist: Please hold on a moment. I'll put you through. I'm afraid Mr. Bennett isn't available. He's in a meeting until three o'clock.
Kate: Sorry, can you speak up, please? I can't hear you very well.
Receptionist: Yes, Mr. Bennett is in a meeting until three o'clock.
Kate: I see. I'd like to leave a message, please.
Receptionist: Of course.
Kate: I need to check the order number for the wedding cake. I have four, seven, two, nine, one, and I want to know if that's correct. Could he email me to confirm? Would you like me to say that again?
Receptionist: Yes, please. Just the order number.
Kate: It's four, seven, two, nine, one.
Receptionist: Thank you. I'll make sure he gets the message.
Kate: Thanks. Goodbye.
Receptionist: Goodbye.
a2-unit-17.17.3 Voicemail: Paulo: Hi, Tom! It's Paulo here. You're not picking up, so I guess you're at school. Since I can't get through to you, I'll leave a message. I'm on the overnight train from New York to Chicago. I'm calling to tell you that I'll be late. I think I should be at Union Station at ten. The train is delayed again. Hang on a minute. They're making an announcement. OK, now it looks like I'll be there at eleven. Did you get that? Eleven o'clock. Can you text me to confirm? We're going through a tunnel, so I'm probably breaking up. Anyway, see you later!
